Option to reduce session number to 3/week or shorten sessions if low energy while breastfeeding

raw_text:
Thanks — useful context. I’ll give a clear 4-week on-ramp (Weeks 1–4) for a client who is 10 weeks postpartum, cleared for moderate exercise, but must avoid impact/jumping for 4 more weeks. Home equipment: bodyweight + light dumbbells (I’ll assume 2–8 kg/5–20 lb range available). Week 1 is an acclimatisation week (lower volume/intensity, focus on breathing, pelvic floor, core, movement quality). Progression across weeks adds load, complexity, and conditioning while still avoiding impact. I’ll include session-by-session plans, sets/reps, tempo cues, breathing/pelvic-floor guidance, recovery, and basic nutrition suggestions relevant to postpartum (if breastfeeding, note calorie needs).

Important safety notes to give to client before starting
- Confirm OB clearance has been received and there are no warning symptoms: heavy bleeding, new or worsening pelvic/abdominal pain, dizziness, fainting, or prolapse sensations. If any of these appear, stop and consult the OB.
- Screen for diastasis recti: teach gentle abdominal connection (see cues below). Avoid Valsalva-heavy maneuvers early.
- Avoid high intra-abdominal pressure and breath-holding during exertion. Emphasise exhale on effort and gentle pelvic-floor engagement.
- Stop or regress any exercise if she feels bulging along midline, heaviness in pelvis, or persistent leaking.

Overall weekly structure (4 weeks)
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (3 strength + 1 active recovery / mobility + optional short walk 2–3x week). You can reduce to 3 strength sessions if she needs extra recovery.
- Session length: 30–40 minutes for strength sessions in Week 1, progressing to 35–50 min by Week 4.
- Equipment: light dumbbells, mat, chair/bench, resistance band (optional).
- Goals by week:
  - Week 1: Acclimatisation, breathing, pelvic-floor re-education, mobility, low-load movement patterns.
  - Week 2: Build strength with slightly higher volume; introduce more loaded pushing/pulling and single-leg basics.
  - Week 3: Increase intensity and strength sets; start short conditioning circuits without impact (low-impact cardio).
  - Week 4: Consolidate gains, progressive overload for main lifts, prepare baseline for next block. Still no jumping.

Pelvic-floor / breathing primer (to practice daily, short sets)
- Diaphragmatic breath: inhale gently through nose letting ribs expand, exhale through mouth while letting ribs draw down. On each exhale perform a gentle pelvic-floor lift (imagine stopping urine, but only a light pull and release). 5–8 slow reps x 2–3 sets per day.
- Abdominal bracing for exercise: inhale to prepare, exhale as you initiate the movement while gently drawing the lower belly toward the spine and a light pelvic-floor lift. Avoid hard bearing down.
- Diastasis modification: if a gap and bulge occur with stronger contractions, reduce load and focus on transversus abdominis activation and progression to curl-ups with breath-and-hollow technique.

Progression and tempo cues
- Use controlled tempos: 3s eccentric, 1s pause, 1s concentric for many exercises early on.
- Aim for RPE 5–7 on strength days (moderate).
- Increase weight or reps each week only if form and pelvic-floor control are pristine.

Week 1 — Acclimatisation (low volume, emphasis on control)
Schedule: 3 strength sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri) + 1 active recovery/mobility (Sun). Optional 15–20 min brisk walk 3x week at conversational pace.

Session A (Lower + core fundamentals) — 30–35 min
- Warm-up 6–8 min: walking or marching on spot 3 min; 2 min hip circles + knee hugs; 1–2 min breathing/pelvic-floor practice.
- Glute bridges (bodyweight): 3 sets x 10 reps, 3s lowering. Cue: breathe out as you lift, brief pelvic-floor engagement.
- Split-stance RDL (rear foot elevated or staggered stance) with light DBs: 3 x 8 each leg. Focus hip hinge, slight knee bend.
- Bodyweight squat to chair (box squat): 3 x 10. Controlled descent 3s; sit lightly then stand. Use hands to assist if needed.
- Heel raises (bilateral): 3 x 12 slow. Balance support as needed.
- Dead bug (progression with heel slide): 3 x 8–10 each side. Control, exhale on effort.
- Side-lying clamshells (band optional): 2 x 12 each side.
- Cool-down 5 min: gentle hamstring/quadriceps/hip flexor stretches + diaphragmatic breathing 1–2 min.

Session B (Upper + posterior chain) — 30–35 min
- Warm-up 6–8 min: marching + arm circles + band pull-aparts light.
- Incline push-ups (hands on counter or wall if needed): 3 x 8–10. Emphasise exhale and core engagement.
- One-arm DB row (supporting hand on chair): 3 x 8 each side.
- Pallof press (anti-rotation) with band or light DB hold across chest pressing out one-handed: 3 x 10s hold each side (or 10 presses slow) — teach core control.
- Seated overhead DB press (light) 3 x 8–10. Use back support if needed.
- Bird-dog (kneeling) 3 x 8 each side (slow, breathe out as you reach).
- Farmer carry (light DBs) 3 x 30–45s walks inside home for grip and posture.
- Cool-down 5 min breathing + pec stretch.

Session C (Mixed mobility & conditioning — low impact) — 30–35 min
- Warm-up: 6 min march, hip openers.
- Circuit 2 rounds, 40s work / 20s rest each:
  - Marching high knees (controlled) or low step-ups on a step
  - Wall or incline push-ups
  - Glute bridge hold (30–40s)
  - Seated band row or bent-over DB row
  - Standing band/DB chop (anti-rotation)
- Finish with 8–10 min mobility + pelvic-floor breathing routine.

Notes Week 1: Keep loads light. Concentrate on regaining motor patterns and breath-teach. Rest as needed between sets (60–90s). If any pelvic heaviness or bulging occurs, reduce intensity and refer back to pelvic-floor exercises.

Week 2 — Build foundation (slightly higher volume, introduce single-leg balance)
Schedule: 3 strength sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri) + 1 mobility/conditioning (Sun). Continue walks.

Session A (Lower focus) — 35–40 min
- Warm-up 6–8 min: marching, leg swings, breathing work.
- Goblet squat with light DB: 3 x 10 (progress from chair squat). Tempo 3:1:1.
- Romanian deadlift with DB (both hands): 3 x 10. Focus hinge, slight knee bend.
- Reverse lunges (static split, alternating): 3 x 8 each leg. Use support if needed.
- Single-leg balance with mini-squat (bodyweight): 2 x 8–10 each side.
- Side plank on knees (core) 3 x 20–30s each side.
- Glute bridge march (alternate knee lifts while holding bridge): 2 x 8–10 each side.
- Cool-down 5–7 min with breathing.

Session B (Upper + core progression) — 35–40 min
- Warm-up 6–8 min.
- Incline to flat push-up progression: 3 x 8 (move to slightly lower incline if possible).
- Two-arm DB row (bent-over) 3 x 10.
- Overhead press 3 x 8–10 (slightly heavier if comfortable).
- Band face pulls 3 x 12.
- Standing single-arm pallof press 3 x 8–10 each side.
- Dead bug with added load (light DB on thighs or hold long enough): 3 x 10 total.
- Cool-down.

Session C (Low-impact conditioning + mobility) — 30–40 min
- Warm-up 6 min.
- Low-impact AMRAP 10–12 min: alternating 30s work/15s rest
  - Step-ups (moderate pace)
  - DB deadlift (light)
  - Seated or incline push-ups
  - Plank on knees (20–30s)
- Mobility circuit 2 rounds (hip flexor stretch, thoracic rotations, calf stretch).
- Finish pelvic-floor breathing.

Week 3 — Progress intensity, introduce heavier sets and single-leg strength
Schedule: 3 strength sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri) + 1 conditioning/mobility. Introduce slightly longer carries and tempo variations.

Session A (Lower strength + hip hinge emphasis) — 40–45 min
- Warm-up 8 min.
- Goblet squat: 4 x 8 (increase DB weight if possible).
- Romanian deadlift single-leg support (RDL with opposite hand touching bench for balance) 3 x 8 each leg.
- Bulgarian split squats (rear foot on low chair) 3 x 6–8 each side — use light DBs.
- Hip thrusts (single or double leg) 3 x 10 (use a chair for back support).
- Calf raises single leg (assisted) 3 x 10 each.
- Ab roll-out progression with band or incline (knees) 3 x 8 (stop if bulging).
- Cool-down + breathing.

Session B (Upper strength + stability) — 40 min
- Warm-up 8 min.
- Push-up progression: 4 x 8 (lower incline or floor if ready).
- One-arm DB row heavier 4 x 8 each side.
- Standing DB press 3 x 8–10.
- Inverted row (under table/low bar) or band row 3 x 8–10.
- Farmer carry heavier 3 x 40–60s.
- Side plank full or knees 3 x 30s.
- Cool-down.

Session C (Conditioning low-impact + core) — 35–40 min
- Warm-up 6–8 min.
- EMOM 15 min (every minute on the minute): alternate two exercises
  - Minute 1: Step-ups x 10 each leg or 40s stepping
  - Minute 2: DB swing (light, hip hinge, not ballistic—use controlled Romanian deadlift to upright) x 12 or 40s RDL-to-stand
- Core finisher: hollow hold 3 x 20s (or modified)
- Mobility + pelvic-floor breathing.

Week 4 — Consolidation and baseline testing (no jumping)
Schedule: 3 strength sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri) + 1 active recovery. Aim to test baseline measures at end of week: e.g., 1) max reps incline push-ups in 60s, 2) max bodyweight squats in 60s, 3) single-leg balance hold time — to set next block.

Session A (Lower + strength test elements) — 45–50 min
- Warm-up 8 min.
- Goblet squat 4 x 6–8 (heavier if form maintained).
- Romanian deadlift 4 x 8 (heavier).
- Reverse lunge walking or stationary 3 x 8 each.
- Hip thrusts 3 x 10–12 with 2s pause at top.
- Single-leg balance + reach (single-leg RDL to touch) 3 x 6–8.
- Cool-down + breathing.

Session B (Upper + posterior chain) — 45 min
- Warm-up 8 min.
- Push-up test (after warm-up): do 1 set of max reps in 60s on an incline—record. Then:
- Incline/flat push-ups 4 x 6–10.
- DB rows 4 x 8.
- Overhead press 3 x 8–10.
- Band pull-aparts or face-pulls 3 x 12.
- Farmer carry 3 x 60s.
- Cool-down.

Session C (Conditioning + mobility) — 35–40 min
- Warm-up 6–8.
- Circuit 3 rounds:
  - 40s step-ups
  - 40s bent-over DB deadlifts
  - 40s incline push-ups
  - 40s plank (knee or full)
  - Rest 60–90s between rounds
- Mobility + pelvic-floor breathing.
- Baseline tests (if desired): max squats 60s, single-leg balance time, record results and note weights used for progression.

Regressions and progressions / modifications
- If pelvic-floor symptoms worsen or bulge appears: regress to lower ROM, less load, more pelvic-floor breathing. Avoid loaded overhead pressing and heavy carries until symptoms resolve.
- For diastasis: avoid full sit-ups/crunches; use curl-up with breath-hollowing and limit load.
- If breastfeeding and feeling low-energy, reduce session number to 3/week or shorten sessions.

Recovery and sleep
- Encourage 7–9 hours sleep where possible; naps when possible with baby to support recovery.
- Prioritise hydration (aim for 2–3 L/day baseline, more if breastfeeding).
- Use foam rolling, gentle stretching and 5–10 minute breathing sessions daily to manage stress.

Nutrition (general postpartum guidance — tailor to breastfeeding status)
- If breastfeeding: don’t restrict calories drastically. Aim for a modest 300–500 kcal/day deficit only if weight loss is a goal and lactation is established. Emphasise protein ~1.2–2.0 g/kg bodyweight per day (or at least 20–30 g protein per meal) to support recovery and milk supply.
- Balanced plates: lean protein, whole grains, healthy fats, vegetables. Snack options: Greek yogurt, nut butter on fruit/toast, cottage cheese and fruit, smoothies with spinach/oats/protein powder if needed.
- Iron and vitamin D: assess dietary intake; many postpartum clients benefit from iron-rich foods and continuation of prenatal vitamins per OB guidance.
- Hydration: breastfeeds increase fluid needs — sip water regularly; have a water bottle during sessions.

Client coaching cues to emphasise
- Exhale on exertion; gentle pelvic-floor lift rather than squeeze-and-hold.
- Quality over quantity: stop sets if breath-holding occurs or a doming/rope appears along midline.
- Movement is gradual: week 1 is about consistency and reeducation.

How to progress after week 4
- Use recorded baseline measures and perceived exertion to design the next 8–12 week block focused on strength and conditioning. Gradually add unilateral loaded work, heavier goblet/front-loaded squats, and higher-intensity low-impact cardio (bike, row) and then reintroduce plyometrics only when cleared by OB and pelvic-floor is stable.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this to a printable week-by-week schedule with checkboxes.
- Adjust sets/reps and exercise choices for specific dumbbell weights you have.
- Provide sample meals / a 7-day postpartum-friendly meal plan (tell me if breastfeeding).

Would you like the plan converted to a printable 4-week calendar or adjusted for specific equipment/weights?
